key_insight: Energy harvesting can enable battery-independent microsystems, but real-world success depends as much on power management and integration as on the transducer materials themselves.
engineering_relevance: The review helps engineers choose and combine TENG, piezoelectric, pyroelectric, indoor PV, and RF harvesting approaches while accounting for cold-start, impedance matching, and storage degradation.
method: Compare major harvesting modalities: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor photovoltaics, RF rectennas
Highlight hybrid multi-source integration strategies and metamaterial-enabled broadband RF harvesting
Survey system-level advances in PMICs, cold-start circuits, and micro-storage reliability
evidence_signal: The abstract cites reported gains such as over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved RF harvesting via multiband/broadband metamaterial architectures.
watch_item: Promising laboratory results may not translate directly to field use because ultra-low-voltage startup, source mismatch, and long-term storage degradation remain unresolved.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
